newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end jittery session lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end jittery session lower.

text.p: U.S. debt futures closed lower on light volume on market jitters ahead of Friday's U.S. employment numbers, traders and analysts said.
They also said a Reuters story that the U.S. Federal Reserve was likely to tighten credit at its March 25 Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) dampened sentiment ahead of Friday's key labor numbers.
An unnamed source close to the Fed was quoted as saying the Fed was likely to inch up the 5.25-percent federal funds rate when it met later in the month.
"The story didn't help market psychology," a trader said.
"But really, there was just a dearth of buying ahead of the reports," he said about the U.S. February nonfarm payrolls number and the unemployment rate.
Payrolls are expected, on average, to rise 230,000, versus 271,000 in January, and the unemployment rate is forecast to fall to 5.3 percent, from 5.4 percent.
"I think the numbers will be unfriendly," Paul Kasriel, chief economist at Northern Trust, said. "I think you'll see gains in average hourly earnings, I think the unemployment rate will be lower."
U.S. jobless claims for the week ended March 10 fell to 310,000 against average forecasts for 317,000 and against the prior week's level of 316,000.
The four-week claims average fell to 310,000 for the lowest level since May 13, 1989.

Although traders said the report confirmed that labor conditions in the U.S. remain tight, the bond futures market held gains. Opening gains were largely attributed to short-term technical factors, including oversold conditions.
June T-bonds climbed to 110-07/32 above Wednesday's high, but relinquished gains and turned lower by midsession.
June T-bonds fell from 109-25/32 to 109-21/32, the 200-day moving average, on active selling, particularly from one major U.S. firm and a large local pit trader.
One Eurodollar futures trader, however, thought the market was turning too negative.
"Tomorrow's numbers could surprise a lot of people," he said.

At the end of pit trade, June T-bonds were off 13/32 at 110-01/32, June T-bills were down 0.020 at 94.73, June Eurodollars were down 0.020 at 94.16, and September Eurodollars were off 0.030 at 93.945. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com))
